facts: The Cabinet approved reclassification of 22.31 acres in Nellore Urban mandal, SPSR Nellore district, for house-site pattas to eligible beneficiaries.

national.headline: India’s team wins nine medals at the 19th International Earth Science Olympiad
facts: India won nine medals at the 19th International Earth Science Olympiad (IESO) 2026: four gold, three silver and two bronze.
The Olympiad was held in Turin, Italy, from 20 to 27 August, with participants from 39 countries.
The Ministry of Earth Sciences said the nine-medal tally was India’s highest in IESO history.
Soumik Mandal of West Bengal won two gold and one silver and ranked third overall among participants from 39 countries.
The national selection test drew approximately 17,800 students across 500 centres; the top 25 attended a training camp at M.S. University, Vadodara.
The 19th IESO 2026 was held under the aegis of the International Geoscience Organisation.
national.summary: On 4 September, the Union Minister for Earth Sciences felicitated India’s student team for its nine-medal performance at IESO 2026. The results highlight the country’s Earth-science education and training pipeline.

national.headline: Supreme Court eCommittee flags off the first 26 Mobile eSewa Vans
facts: The Supreme Court eCommittee, NALSA and the Department of Justice flagged off 26 Mobile eSewa Vans on 4 September.
The 26 vans form the first tranche of a planned fleet of 73 vans for designated High Court and district-court jurisdictions.
The initiative extends eCourts services, legal aid and dispute-resolution access to citizens, including people in remote and underserved areas.
The vans are intended to support services including digital e-filing, secure e-payments, Mobile Lok Adalats and legal-literacy programmes.

facts: The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment reported the inauguration of NAMASTE card issuance to waste pickers in the MCD Najafgarh Zone on 4 September.
Ayushman cards were also distributed to participating waste pickers.

NAMASTE is a Central Sector Scheme focused on sanitation-worker safety, formal recognition, healthcare and social-security access, skills and mechanisation of hazardous sanitation work.

international.headline: WHO validates Bhutan’s elimination of dog-transmitted human rabies
facts: On 4 September, WHO validated Bhutan’s elimination of dog-transmitted rabies as a public-health problem; Bhutan became the first country in the WHO South-East Asia Region to receive this validation.

Bhutan plans to sustain free PEP access across all 20 districts and strengthen cross-border coordination with neighbouring Indian states.

international.headline: UN General Assembly adopts resolution urging more equitable map representation
facts: On 4 September, the UN General Assembly adopted resolution A/80/L.104, titled “Correct the Map”, by 164 votes to one, with six abstentions.
The resolution encourages governments, schools, international organisations and technology companies to use equal-area projections, such as Equal Earth, when relative land area matters.
It does not ban the Mercator projection or mandate a single replacement map.
Togo led the initiative on behalf of the African Group, with African Union backing.
international.summary: The resolution calls attention to how map projections can distort the apparent relative size of continents and encourages use of equal-area maps where area comparison matters. It is non-binding encouragement: it neither prohibits Mercator maps nor requires one alternative projection.

international.prelimsTakeaway: Mercator preserves direction for navigation but distorts relative area; Equal Earth is an equal-area alternative cited in the UN discussion.
international.mainsAngle: Discuss how choices in representation can influence geographic understanding, while distinguishing the educational and symbolic debate from the technical purposes of different map projections.

international.headline: UNFCCC announces Baku Climate Week support for Paris Agreement transparency reporting
facts: On 4 September, UN Climate Change announced activities in Baku during UNFCCC Climate Week 4 to support implementation of the Paris Agreement’s Enhanced Transparency Framework (ETF).
UNFCCC, UNEP, UNDP, FAO, CBIT-GSP and the Baku Transparency Platform were identified as partners in the effort.
A high-level dialogue was scheduled to begin on 7 September, followed by technical workshops from 8–10 September to assist countries preparing their second-round Biennial Transparency Reports.
UNFCCC stated that the second-round reports were due by 31 December 2026; the 4 September release announced planned activities, not their completion.
international.summary: The announcement set out planned political and technical support for countries working on Paris Agreement transparency reporting. The focus was ETF implementation and practical assistance with Biennial Transparency Reports ahead of the 31 December 2026 deadline.
